item.title: Deep Sequence Model Reveals Disrupted Emotion‑Action Coupling in Adolescents with NSSI
item.description:
Deep Sequence Model Reveals Disrupted Emotion‑Action Coupling in Adolescents with NSSI

A new AI study submitted on 8 Oct 2026 combines an experimental pain paradigm, EEG microstate analysis, and an interpretable deep sequence model to uncover neurodynamic mechanisms linking social distress to non‑suicidal self‑injury (NSSI) in depressed adolescents.

🔍 Overview

  • Study population: 106 adolescents with depression (67 with NSSI, labeled DN+; 39 without NSSI, labeled DN-).
  • Conditions examined: social pain, physical pain, and resting‑state.
  • Goal: Identify brain‑state dynamics that differentiate DN+ from DN- during social pain.

🧩 How it works

  • Data acquisition: High‑density EEG recorded while participants experienced social and physical pain stimuli.
  • Microstate analysis: EEG segmented into recurring topographic patterns (microstates) labeled MS3, MS5, etc.
  • Deep sequence model: Integrated disease‑specific, domain‑adversarial, consistency, and contrastive learning objectives to capture higher‑order dependencies in microstate sequences.

⚙️ Key details

  • Classification performance: Social‑pain condition achieved 68.55% accuracy in distinguishing DN+ from DN-, an 8.94‑point improvement over the best baseline.
  • Neurodynamic findings:
    • DN+ adolescents showed weakened bidirectional transitions between MS3 and MS5 during social pain.
    • Source reconstruction linked MS3 to emotional/interoceptive processing and MS5 to action preparation, indicating disrupted emotion‑action coupling.
    • Time‑resolved analysis revealed:
      • Greater early‑to‑middle recruitment of action‑related states.
      • Later recruitment of emotion‑related states in DN+ participants.
  • Mediation patterns:
    • In DN- adolescents, MS5‑to‑MS3 dynamics mediated the link between social‑evaluation sensitivity and affective outcomes.
    • This mediation was absent in DN+ adolescents, while MS3‑to‑MS5 transitions correlated with increased negative affect in DN+.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a mechanistically interpretable neural signature for objective identification of NSSI.
  • Highlights disrupted emotion‑action coupling as a core neurodynamic mechanism in adolescents experiencing social pain.
  • Demonstrates the utility of interpretable deep sequence modeling for uncovering higher‑order brain‑state dependencies in clinical neuroscience.

#NSSI #EEG #DeepLearning #Neuroscience #AI

Source: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury

item.title: OpenAI publicist pushes to change interview after suicide discussion
item.description:
OpenAI publicist pushes to change interview after suicide discussion

An OpenAI publicist tried to change the topic of CEO Sam Altman’s interview with Vanity Fair’s Mark Guiducci after the editor brought up a ChatGPT user’s suicide.

When Guiducci confronted Altman about the incident, the publicist warned Guiducci about running out of time, saying she’d like to “move on” to another topic.

“These are some of the hardest questions that we face or that anybody developing this technology faces,” Altman said.

The interruption came shortly after Guiducci asked Altman if he knew who Laura Reiley is, a journalist who wrote an essay for The New York Times about her daughter’s conversations with ChatGPT before she took her own life.

“Her daughter committed suicide after speaking to ChatGPT. ChatGPT did not tell her to kill herself—” Guiducci said just before the publicist interrupted him.

“Mark, we have two minutes left. I want to be respectful, but I’d like to move on and talk a little bit about the future and what’s coming,” the publicist said.

Even after Guiducci explained that he’s going to finish the question and then “go back to what we were talking about,” the publicist pushed back.

“We really actually have to walk out the door in one or two minutes,” she said.

Despite the pushback, the interview continued with Guiducci asking Altman whether the company planned to use conversations with ChatGPT to shape policies surrounding its response to a user’s mental health crisis.

“You know, should we release people’s private data and some of their hardest moments to researchers? I think probably not without their consent. Or I should say, not without their consent.”

When reached for comment about the interruption, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said: “The interview was running over, which is why we ultimately asked to schedule even more time to continue the conversation after Sam addressed this critically important topic.”

Crisis Resources

  • If you or someone you know is considering suicide or is anxious, depressed, upset, or needs to talk, there are people who want to help.
  • Crisis Text Line: Text HOME to 741-741 from anywhere in the US, at any time, about any type of crisis.
  • 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: Call or text 988 (formerly known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline).
  • The original phone number, 1-800-273-TALK (8255), is available as well.
  • The Trevor Project: Text START to 678-678 or call 1-866-488-7386 at any time to speak to a trained counselor.
  • The International Association for Suicide Prevention lists a number of suicide hotlines by country. Click here to find them.
  • Befrienders Worldwide has a network of crisis helplines active in 48 countries. Click here to find them.

#OpenAI #SamAltman #ChatGPT #MentalHealth

Source: OpenAI PR tells journalist to ‘move on’ while asking Sam Altman about a ChatGPT user’s suicide
